compute.note: parameters = alpha N^2 + alpha N + N = 1*196^2 + 1*196 + 196 = 38808 real (float32) parameters: nk.models.RBM is a dense RBM (Dense kernel N x alpha N, hidden bias alpha N, visible bias N; both biases on by NetKet default, alpha = --features = 1), no weight sharing across translations. samples = 1024 per optimisation step (MCState n_samples = batch_size; MetropolisExchange with n_chains = batch_size = 1024, one sample per chain per step, each separated by sweep_size = N = 196 proposals (NetKet default), n_discard_per_chain = 0); iterations = 10000 ("--max_step" default=10**4); optimizer SR (VMC_SRt when n_parameters >= n_samples), lr 1e-3. The final energy is then estimated once with estim_size = 1024^2 = 1048576 samples (not an optimisation step). NetKet pinned twice by the program: programs/vmc_netket/requirements.txt "NetKet==3.13.0" and conda_env.yaml "netket=3.11.4"; every NetKet line cited here reads the same at both tags. The energy is older than the script: VarBench's data file listed it with no code link ("TODO: own code", varbench/varbench 0ef1497c and 6e9f6b83, 2024-07-11) until the scripts were added on 2024-07-30 (5047bfd6 RBM, d54f7c01 RNN, 765c5d13 GCNN), which changed only the reference column, so the script documents the settings after the fact, with library versions that may postdate the run.

compute.note: Parameters evaluated: NetKet 3.13.0 Jastrow stores the strictly lower triangle of W, N(N-1)/2 = 196*195/2 = 19110 real (float32) weights, which is also what vmc.py prints as n_params (tree_size_real_nonzero). Samples: 1024 per SR step, 1024 chains of length 1, each sample one sweep of 196 exchange proposals, no discard. Iterations: 10^4 steps (--max_step default). Driver: nkx.driver.VMC_SRt (n_parameters >= n_samples = 1024). After training the energy is estimated from 2^20 samples. stored sigma 0.011 vs sqrt(stored variance 136.877 / 2^20) = 0.011: consistent with the script's 2^20-sample final estimate (--estim_size default). Provenance: the value entered VarBench in 59e621a (2022-09-13, Dian Wu); the linked script was added to varbench/methods in c686621 (2024-07-30) without the value changing, so the script is the authors' later reconstruction of the baseline, not a log of the run (the same holds for the TFIsing RBM rows, scripts/defects.mjs). The 2^20-sample final estimate is corroborated by the stored sigma; batch size and step count are not independently corroborated. No device or time is recorded (the conda env includes CUDA; the README says a GPU is "usually needed for VMC on larger lattices", which is not a statement about these runs).
